vulnerability.title: Django applies FILE_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS only to the leaf directory, creating intermediate upload and collectstatic directories world-accessible on Python 3.7+
vulnerability.category_l2: incorrect default permissions on intermediate upload, storage and collectstatic directories

fix_commits.message: Fixed CVE-2020-24583, #31921 -- Fixed permissions on intermediate-level static and storage directories on Python 3.7+.
[3.1.x] Fixed CVE-2020-24583, #31921 -- Fixed permissions on intermediate-level static and storage directories on Python 3.7+.
[3.0.x] Fixed CVE-2020-24583, #31921 -- Fixed permissions on intermediate-level static and storage directories on Python 3.7+.
[2.2.x] Fixed CVE-2020-24583, #31921 -- Fixed permissions on intermediate-level static and storage directories on Python 3.7+.

vulnerability.vulnerable_commit_basis: tag 3.0.2 points directly at a3697439; the 3.0.9 storage.py blob is byte-identical to 3.0.2 and to the fix parent db8b9357, while the 3.0.10 blob differs, so 3.0.2 carries the unfixed _save implementation

critical_operation.code_excerpt:
if self.directory_permissions_mode is not None:
                # os.makedirs applies the global umask, so we reset it,
                # for consistency with file_permissions_mode behavior.
                old_umask = os.umask(0)
                try:
                    os.makedirs(directory, self.directory_permissions_mode, exist_ok=True)
                finally:
                    os.umask(old_umask)
critical_operation.description: FileSystemStorage._save creates the upload target directory by temporarily setting the process umask to 0 and calling os.makedirs(directory, self.directory_permissions_mode). On Python 3.7+ os.makedirs applies the mode argument only to the leaf directory; intermediate-level directories are created with 0o777 masked only by the ambient umask. Because the code sets the umask to 0, every intermediate directory is created world-readable, world-writable and world-executable (0o777), ignoring FILE_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS. The same _save implementation serves uploads and, through StaticFilesStorage, the collectstatic command, so both intermediate upload directories and intermediate collected static directories are affected. The 3.0.10/2.2.16/3.1.1 fix sets the umask to 0o777 & ~self.directory_permissions_mode so intermediates receive exactly the configured mode.

entry_point.description: An upload (or collectstatic run) supplies a destination name with one or more not-yet-existing parent directories; _save resolves the full path and creates the directory tree.

trace.description: directory_permissions_mode resolves the explicit storage argument or settings.FILE_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS
the explicitly configured mode is passed as the makedirs mode argument
the process umask is set to 0 before makedirs, so intermediate directories get 0o777 instead of the configured mode
collectstatic reaches the same _save because StaticFilesStorage inherits FileSystemStorage

source_crosscheck.notes: The Django announcement, NVD and OSV/GHSA agree on the three affected ranges, the fixed releases 2.2.16/3.0.10/3.1.1 and the root cause in intermediate-directory permissions. The MITRE CNA record is a placeholder. NVD assigns CWE-276 and CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH. Upstream blob identity ties 3.0.2 and 3.0.9 to the fix parent content. The three backport commits cite a master commit ea0febbba that is not reachable in the public repository; the advisory-listed master changeset 8d727157 was verified instead and first appears in tag 3.2a1.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read FileSystemStorage._save at 3.0.2 and confirm the umask(0)/makedirs interaction and the Python 3.7+ intermediate-directory behaviour.
An independent reviewer must confirm 08892bff is absent from 3.0.2 and 3.0.9 and an ancestor of 3.0.10, and that 3.0.10 storage.py contains the new umask expression.
An independent reviewer must confirm the 2.2.16 and 3.1.1 fixes and the three release boundaries against a second source family.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No filesystem permission experiment, upload, collectstatic run or Django test suite was executed; the finding is static.
The Python 3.7+ os.makedirs intermediate-directory behaviour is taken from the advisory and the fixed comment; it was not reproduced locally.
The impact requires a local attacker or co-tenant on the same filesystem; remote exploitation depends on the deployment layout and is not claimed.
The MITRE CVE v5 CNA record is a placeholder (vendor/product/version n/a, problemType n/a, no CVSS).
NVD also carries a CVSS 2.0 metric of 5.0; the canonical score follows the NVD primary CVSS 3.1 metric.

The three backport commits state "Backport of ea0febbba531a3ecc8c77b570efbfb68ca7155db from master", but that object is not reachable in the public django/django clone and the advisory lists 8d727157 as the master changeset. The master-side change was verified through 8d727157, which first appears in tag 3.2a1.
No downstream distribution backport (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Oracle, NetApp) was verified; only upstream tags and commits are used.
The snapshot inventory status is NEEDS_REVIEW with 67 ambiguous files, not a clean PASS.
open_questions: Whether specific deployments expose intermediate directories to untrusted local users was not surveyed.
The exact CPython change that made os.makedirs stop applying mode to intermediate directories was not traced; only its effect is described.
The sibling CVE-2020-24584 (file system cache permissions) is recorded as a separate candidate and is not covered here.
